subject: Comp bands & geo adjustments — proposal for Q2 rollout
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Compensation bands and geo adjustments for 2026 Q2 rollout

Team —

Attached is v3 of the comp band spreadsheet (named comp-band-proposal-v3.xlsx). High-level goals here: align leveling across Eng/Product, tighten overlap between L3/L4, and add geo multipliers for EU and APAC hires. Key asks:

- Please review Level definitions (tab: leveling) — I pushed suggested duties and examples for L2-L6. If we keep the narrower overlap it reduces offer negotiation room but improves internal equity.
- Geo bands: suggested multipliers are listed on tab: geo-bands (US baseline = 1.0). I flagged regions where market data is sparse.
- Benchmarking: I requested a short report from Mercer; will add when it arrives.
- Headcount impact: assuming hires at midpoint of bands, the Cost tab shows a ~6% qtrly bump if we adopt the mid-range recommendations.

Timeline: please send comments in-line by EOD Mon Mar 9. If no major flags, I propose we sign off week of Mar 9–13 so People Ops can update offer templates before new reqs open.

Attachments: [attachment: comp-band-proposal-v3.xlsx]

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Mercer Compensation <bench@mercer.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Draft: Compensation bands and geo adjustments for 2026 Q2 rollout

Laura / team —

Attached is a concise benchmarking packet (Mercer-benchmarks-2025.pdf). We pulled 2025 regional medians and the 60/75/90 percentiles across Software Eng IC roles and Product managers. Quick highlights:

- US (national median) aligns with your baseline; SF/SV 75th percentile is ~18–22% above national median for senior ICs.
- EU (remote hires in EU) shows a 12–16% lower median vs US baseline, but local markets (London, Berlin) are within 5% of national median.
- APAC data is noisy — Singapore and Sydney trend closer to US medians for senior roles; other markets lag 20%+.

Recommendation: For global consistency, set US baseline = comp band median; apply region multipliers as a band (e.g., EU: 0.88–0.92, APAC: 0.80–1.05 depending on city). We can refine by role if you send a short list of target cities/reqs.

Attachment: [attachment: Mercer-benchmarks-2025.pdf]

— Tom Graves
Mercer Compensation Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Compensation bands and geo adjustments for 2026 Q2 rollout

Thanks Laura — quick read-through and my notes inline below.

On Thu, 05 Mar 2026 at 09:12, Laura Bennett wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Attached is v3 of the comp band spreadsheet (named comp-band-proposal-v3.xlsx). High-level goals here: align leveling across Eng/Product, tighten overlap between L3/L4, and add geo multipliers for EU and APAC hires.

My take: I agree with tightening overlap for L3-L4 (reduces salary compression). Suggested edits: shift L3 midpoint down 4% and L4 midpoint up 3% to reduce the 10% overlap to ~3%. That preserves promotion leverage.

On the geo multipliers — after Mercer’s notes, I propose: EU multiplier = 0.90 (band span +/- 4%), APAC = 0.92 for SG/SYD and 0.80 for low-cost APAC hubs. I added a small per-role addendum for Senior PMs on the spreadsheet.

Headcount ask: If we greenlight these bands, I propose we open 5 new IC reqs this quarter (3 Eng, 2 Product). I attached a quick headcount hit file with estimates (updated-headcount-headroom.xlsx). Estimated incremental comp run-rate at midpoint = $620k annualized.

Attachments: [attachment: updated-headcount-headroom.xlsx]

Next steps I recommend:
- Rishi to confirm budget sign-off and whether reserves exist for uplift.
- Olga to coordinate legal review on offer language for geo-specific language (tax/benefits notes).
- Laura to confirm final band table and publish to HR Drive.

Marissa
Director, Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Comp bands & geo multipliers approved for Q2 (action items)

Team —

Thank you for the fast turn around. Decision: approve the comp band updates and geo multipliers as recommended with the following specifics:

- Leveling: implement the tightened L3/L4 overlap per Marissa’s edits (L3 midpoint -4%, L4 midpoint +3%).
- Geo multipliers: EU = 0.90 band (±4%), APAC = 0.92 for SG/SYD, 0.80 for low-cost APAC hubs.
- Headcount: approve opening 5 reqs this quarter as requested (3 Eng, 2 Product). Budget impact acknowledged (estimated annualized comp run-rate +$620k).

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- People Ops (Dev) — update offer templates and HRIS bands by Mar 19. [Dev: please ping me when done.]
- Rishi — provide formal budget sign-off and route to Finance by EOD Mon Mar 15.
- Olga — submit a short compliance note on geo language and any employment terms differences by Mar 16.
- Marissa — publish the final comp-band-final-2026Q2.xlsx to the HR Drive and send an announcement to hiring managers once HRIS is updated.

Attachments: [attachment: comp-band-final-2026Q2.xlsx]

If anything materially changes after budget sign-off we’ll reconvene, but otherwise publish and start using the new bands for offers effective immediately for newly opened reqs.

Laura Bennett
Head of Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference
